agenda: The situation between Iraq and Kuwait
penholder: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland
members: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland

steps.by: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland
steps.intent: The UK’s objective is to keep the Council focused on the remaining humanitarian and property obligations from Iraq’s invasion of Kuwait while welcoming the closure of the UNCC and preserving consensus. The draft presses Iraq on missing persons and national archives without introducing new Chapter VII measures, which should keep Russia and China on board. Difficult points will be language on access and archives, which Iraq may resist, and balancing Kuwaiti concerns with Iraq’s sensitivity over sovereignty; we may need to soften “full access” if necessary.

messages.Algeria: Algeria supports the draft's balanced emphasis on sovereignty, dialogue and the humanitarian obligations concerning missing persons and property. We would like the text to acknowledge more explicitly Iraq's cooperation and to add a constructive reference to international technical assistance and capacity-building. With those adjustments, Algeria can support the text.
messages.China: China thanks the United Kingdom for the draft and supports its overall direction, which is balanced and consistent with relevant Council resolutions. We propose adding language on constructive international support to Iraq and Kuwait, and specifying that the Secretary-General’s reporting be prepared in consultation with the two Governments. With these refinements, China can join consensus.
messages.Denmark: Denmark supports the draft’s renewed focus on missing Kuwaiti and third-country nationals, missing property, and the tripartite mechanism. We ask the penholder to strengthen OP3 with standard humanitarian access language and to reflect the right of families to know the fate and whereabouts of missing persons. We can also support a minor addition to OP6 requiring reporting on obstacles to progress.
messages.France: France supports the current balanced text. It welcomes the continued Iraq-Kuwait cooperation and the emphasis on missing persons, property and archives, as well as the reaffirmation of sovereignty and the reporting role of the Secretary-General. France sees no need for changes at this stage and encourages the Council to adopt the text.
messages.Greece: Greece supports the draft as presented. It reflects the Council’s continued commitment to the sovereignty and territorial integrity of Iraq and Kuwait and to the full implementation of resolution 2107 (2013), especially on missing persons and missing property, including the national archives. We welcome the balanced focus on cooperation with the ICRC and the tripartite mechanism and have no changes to request at this stage.
messages.Guyana: Guyana thanks the United Kingdom for the balanced draft and supports the current text. We attach particular importance to the reaffirmation of the sovereignty, territorial integrity and political independence of Iraq and Kuwait and to the call for peaceful resolution of outstanding issues. We encourage continued cooperation with the ICRC and the tripartite mechanism and are ready to join consensus.
messages.Pakistan: Pakistan thanks the United Kingdom for preparing a balanced draft that is consistent with resolutions 2107 (2013) and 2621 (2022). We welcome its emphasis on the sovereignty, territorial integrity and inviolability of Iraq and Kuwait, and on continued cooperation through the tripartite mechanism and the ICRC. Pakistan has no amendments at this stage and encourages the Council to adopt the text by consensus.
messages.Panama: Panama supports the draft as a balanced and consensus-oriented text. It appropriately focuses on missing persons and property, reaffirms the sovereignty and territorial integrity of Iraq and Kuwait, and maintains useful reporting by the Secretary-General. We have no changes to request at this stage.
messages.Republic of Korea: The Republic of Korea supports the current draft, which reaffirms Iraq's outstanding obligations under resolution 2107 (2013) while encouraging continued Iraq-Kuwait dialogue and confidence-building. We appreciate the penholder's inclusive approach and would join consensus on the text as circulated.
messages.Russian Federation: The Russian Federation supports the draft in principle and welcomes its balanced focus on missing persons and missing property. We request two technical adjustments: in OP3, access should be facilitated in accordance with national legislation and bilateral arrangements with Kuwait; in OP6, the Secretary-General’s reporting should be prepared in close consultation with both Governments. These changes preserve sovereignty and keep the process bilateral and non-politicized.
messages.Sierra Leone: Sierra Leone supports the current balanced text and thanks the United Kingdom for its work as penholder. We believe the draft properly reaffirms the sovereignty of Iraq and Kuwait and maintains focus on the humanitarian obligations concerning missing persons and missing property. Sierra Leone encourages Council unity and consensus on this important matter.
messages.Slovenia: Slovenia supports the current text. It reflects the Council's long-standing emphasis on clarifying the fate of missing persons, returning Kuwaiti property and archives, and maintaining close cooperation with Kuwait, ICRC and the tripartite mechanism. We encourage the penholder to keep the reporting requirement and focus on full implementation.
messages.Somalia: Somalia supports the draft as a balanced and technical follow-up that is consistent with the Council’s previous positions. We welcome the reaffirmation of Iraq’s and Kuwait’s sovereignty, territorial integrity, political independence and inviolability, as well as the emphasis on non-interference and continued cooperation through the tripartite mechanism and the ICRC. We encourage the penholder to retain these elements and stand ready to join consensus.
messages.United States of America: The United States supports the United Kingdom's draft as a balanced text that reaffirms Iraq's obligations under resolution 2107 (2013), including on missing Kuwaiti and third-country nationals and missing Kuwaiti property, including the national archives. We welcome its call for continued cooperation with Kuwait, the ICRC and the tripartite mechanism and for sustained Secretary-General reporting. We see no need for changes at this stage and encourage the Council to adopt the text promptly.

messages.Algeria: Algeria thanks the penholder for incorporating its previous requests, in particular the acknowledgement of Iraq’s cooperation in OP3 and the technical-assistance language in OP6. The current text is balanced and reaffirms the sovereignty, territorial integrity and political independence of Iraq and Kuwait while supporting a peaceful, cooperative approach to outstanding humanitarian issues. Algeria therefore supports the draft as it stands and is ready to vote in favour.
messages.China: China thanks the penholder for incorporating its earlier suggestions. The current text is balanced, reaffirms the sovereignty and territorial integrity of Iraq and Kuwait, and supports Iraq-Kuwait cooperation through the tripartite mechanism and the ICRC. China supports the draft as it stands and encourages consensus adoption, with continued emphasis on dialogue, non-interference and constructive international support.
messages.Denmark: Denmark thanks the penholder for incorporating its earlier amendments on safe and unhindered access, the right of families to know the fate and whereabouts of missing persons, and reporting on obstacles. We consider the current text balanced and implementation-focused, and we are prepared to support it as drafted. Denmark encourages continued constructive engagement between Iraq and Kuwait and remains committed to the Council staying actively seized of the matter.
messages.France: France supports the revised text and thanks the United Kingdom as penholder. We welcome the reaffirmation of Iraq’s obligations under resolution 2107 (2013), including on missing Kuwaiti and third-country nationals and missing Kuwaiti property, including the national archives, as well as continued six-month reporting by the Secretary-General. France encourages Iraq and Kuwait to sustain constructive dialogue and cooperation with the ICRC and the tripartite mechanism, and is ready to vote in favour.
messages.Greece: Greece supports the current text and has no changes to request. We welcome its balanced emphasis on Iraq’s obligations under resolution 2107 (2013), the continuing tripartite and ICRC cooperation, and the sovereignty and territorial integrity of Iraq and Kuwait. We also support the six-month reporting request as a useful transparency and confidence-building measure, and Greece is ready to join consensus.
messages.Guyana: Guyana supports the current text. It is balanced, reaffirms the sovereignty and territorial integrity of both Iraq and Kuwait, and maintains constructive Council engagement on missing persons, missing property and confidence-building. We have no further changes and encourage consensus adoption.
messages.Pakistan: Pakistan supports the revised draft as currently presented. It is balanced, reaffirms the sovereignty and territorial integrity of Iraq and Kuwait, encourages continued cooperation on missing persons and property, and maintains useful reporting by the Secretary-General. We have no further changes and encourage the Council to adopt the text by consensus.
messages.Panama: Panama supports the current text. It reflects the need for full implementation of resolution 2107 (2013), respect for the sovereignty and territorial integrity of Iraq and Kuwait, and continued constructive engagement between the parties. messages.Republic of Korea: The Republic of Korea supports the current text as balanced and consistent with previous Council decisions, including resolution 2107 (2013). We welcome the draft’s reaffirmation of Iraq’s outstanding obligations on missing persons and missing property, including the national archives, and its emphasis on continued constructive dialogue between Iraq and Kuwait. We also support the continuation of six-monthly reporting by the Secretary-General. No further changes are requested.
messages.Russian Federation: The Russian Federation supports the revised draft and will join consensus. messages.Sierra Leone: Sierra Leone supports the current text as a balanced and constructive basis for the Council’s continued engagement on this agenda item. We welcome the emphasis on the sovereignty and territorial integrity of Iraq and Kuwait, the humanitarian imperative of locating missing persons and property, and the importance of continued cooperation through the tripartite mechanism and the International Committee of the Red Cross. We encourage the Council to maintain consensus and remain actively seized of the matter.
messages.Slovenia: Slovenia supports the current text. It is balanced, reaffirms the relevant obligations on missing persons and missing property, including the national archives, and preserves the Council’s regular reporting role. We welcome the continued cooperation between Iraq and Kuwait and the tripartite mechanism, and we see no need for further changes at this stage.
messages.Somalia: Somalia supports the current draft and welcomes the balanced focus on humanitarian obligations, missing persons and property, and the sovereignty and territorial integrity of Iraq and Kuwait. We appreciate the penholder’s constructive approach and have no changes to request at this stage. Somalia encourages continued dialogue and cooperation between Iraq and Kuwait and remains ready to support consensus.
messages.United States of America: The United States supports the current text and commends the United Kingdom for a balanced draft. We welcome its focus on Iraq-Kuwait cooperation, the full implementation of obligations on missing persons and missing property, and continued Secretary-General reporting. We see no need for further changes and support prompt adoption.

steps.summary: All Council members expressed support and requested no changes. The penholder retains the balanced revision 1 text unchanged. The draft is expected to be adopted unanimously.

reasons.Algeria: Algeria’s established policy favours Council unity, respect for the sovereignty of Iraq and Kuwait, and peaceful resolution of outstanding bilateral and humanitarian issues; the draft aligns with these priorities and its prior support on this agenda item. No elements of the text conflict with Algeria’s national interests or foreign-policy record.
reasons.China: China has consistently supported Council resolutions on Iraq and Kuwait and participated constructively in the consensus on this draft. The text reaffirms sovereignty and promotes peaceful resolution of outstanding humanitarian issues without imposing new coercive measures.
reasons.Denmark: Denmark supports the draft, which aligns with its commitment to international law, humanitarian concerns, and continued UN engagement on missing persons and property. There are no concerns that would warrant abstention or opposition.
reasons.France: France has consistently supported consensus resolutions on Iraq and Kuwait and backs continued implementation of missing persons and property obligations under resolution 2107 (2013). The draft imposes no new coercive measures and aligns with France’s support for UN reporting and peaceful bilateral resolution.
reasons.Greece: Greece supported the draft in the last negotiation round and made no requests, so it has no reason to break consensus. The text aligns with Greece’s support for Iraq-Kuwait cooperation, missing persons and property obligations, and full implementation of resolution 2107 (2013).
reasons.Guyana: Guyana supported the draft in the last negotiation round without requesting changes, and the text aligns with Guyana’s consistent support for peaceful settlement, sovereignty, and constructive UN engagement between Iraq and Kuwait.
reasons.Pakistan: Pakistan has consistently supported Council texts promoting Iraq-Kuwait cooperation, sovereignty, and implementation of outstanding obligations, and it supported this draft in the last negotiation round. There is no policy basis for opposing or abstaining.
reasons.Panama: Panama supported the draft in the last negotiation round and has no objections to its emphasis on sovereignty, peaceful resolution, and continued cooperation between Iraq and Kuwait. Since no concerns were raised, Panama votes in favour without making a statement.
reasons.Republic of Korea: The Republic of Korea has consistently supported Council resolutions on Iraq and Kuwait and previously voted in favour of this agenda item. The draft is consistent with Seoul’s support for peaceful dispute resolution, sovereignty, and continued UN engagement on missing persons and property.
reasons.Russian Federation: The draft is a balanced, routine follow-up to resolution 2621 (2022), reaffirming Iraqi and Kuwaiti obligations and continued UN reporting; the Russian Federation had already indicated support and has no objections. There is no need for a pre-vote statement.
reasons.Sierra Leone: Sierra Leone’s last-round position was support and it raised no changes, so the delegation would vote in favour of this balanced text on continued Iraq–Kuwait cooperation and implementation of outstanding obligations. No explanation before the vote is necessary in this near-consensus setting.
reasons.Slovenia: Slovenia supports the draft as a routine, consensus-oriented follow-up to resolution 2107 (2013), consistent with its commitment to international law, humanitarian obligations, and cooperation between Iraq and Kuwait. With no requested changes and broad support among Council members, it would vote in favour without needing to explain its vote before the vote.
reasons.Somalia: Somalia supports the consensus draft, which advances humanitarian cooperation, missing persons and property issues, and the sovereignty of Iraq and Kuwait without imposing new obligations. No statement is necessary.
reasons.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom is the penholder and has consistently supported Council action on Iraq-Kuwait missing persons and property, including resolution 2107. Voting in favour advances UK policy on international law, humanitarian accountability, and regional stability.
reasons.United States of America: The draft reaffirms existing obligations and reporting on Iraq-Kuwait humanitarian issues without imposing new measures, consistent with U.S. support for continued cooperation and previous unanimous Council action. No pre-vote explanation is needed as the United States supports adoption.

before.Algeria: Algeria will vote in favour of the draft resolution. We welcome the continued cooperation between Iraq and Kuwait and the progress achieved through the tripartite mechanism and the International Committee of the Red Cross on the question of missing persons and missing property. Algeria reaffirms the sovereignty, territorial integrity, political independence and inviolability of both Iraq and Kuwait, and stresses that outstanding issues must be resolved peacefully, through dialogue and confidence-building, and without interference in internal affairs. We support continued reporting by the Secretary-General and encourage international technical assistance and capacity-building. Our vote reflects our support for the humanitarian dimension of this file, in particular the right of families to know the fate and whereabouts of their missing loved ones.
before.Denmark: Denmark will vote in favour of this draft resolution. We welcome the continued cooperation between Iraq and Kuwait, including through the tripartite mechanism and the International Committee of the Red Cross, and the progress made in locating and repatriating the remains of missing persons. Denmark stresses the importance of full implementation of resolution 2107 (2013), in particular Iraq’s obligations to locate, recover and return all missing Kuwaiti and third-country nationals and missing Kuwaiti property, including the national archives. We support continued reporting by the Secretary-General and reaffirm the sovereignty, territorial integrity, political independence and inviolability of Iraq and Kuwait.
before.Pakistan: Pakistan welcomes the continued cooperation between Iraq and Kuwait and the progress achieved, including on missing persons and missing property. We reaffirm the sovereignty, territorial integrity, political independence and inviolability of both Iraq and Kuwait, and we support continued constructive dialogue and implementation of the relevant obligations, including resolution 2107 (2013). Pakistan will vote in favour of this draft resolution.
before.Republic of Korea: The Republic of Korea will vote in favour of the draft resolution. We welcome the continued cooperation between Iraq and Kuwait, including through the tripartite mechanism and the International Committee of the Red Cross, and the progress made on missing persons. We reaffirm the importance of full implementation of the relevant Security Council resolutions, in particular resolution 2107 (2013), including obligations relating to missing Kuwaiti and third-country nationals and missing Kuwaiti property, including the national archives. We encourage Iraq and Kuwait to sustain constructive dialogue and confidence-building and support continued six-monthly reporting by the Secretary-General so that the Council can follow progress, including on remaining obstacles and ways to accelerate international technical assistance and capacity-building.
before.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom will vote in favour of this draft resolution, which we were pleased to submit. It reaffirms the Council’s enduring commitment to the sovereignty, territorial integrity and political independence of Iraq and Kuwait, and to the full implementation of resolution 2107 (2013), particularly on missing Kuwaiti and third-country nationals and missing Kuwaiti property, including the national archives. We welcome the cooperation shown by Iraq and Kuwait, and the role of the International Committee of the Red Cross and the tripartite mechanism. We call on Iraq to continue and intensify its efforts, including by providing full, safe and unhindered access to relevant sites, information and archives. We also believe that continued United Nations reporting and support for confidence-building between Iraq and Kuwait remain valuable. We encourage all members to support this resolution.

after.China: China voted in favour of the draft resolution just adopted. We welcome the continued cooperation between Iraq and Kuwait and the progress achieved through the tripartite mechanism and the International Committee of the Red Cross on the question of missing persons and missing property. We support the full implementation of resolution 2107 (2013), including the obligations relating to missing Kuwaiti and third-country nationals and missing Kuwaiti property, including the national archives. China appreciates the efforts of Iraq and Kuwait and encourages both sides to maintain constructive dialogue and confidence-building, resolve outstanding issues peacefully through consultation, and respect the sovereignty, territorial integrity, political independence and inviolability of both countries. The international community should continue to provide constructive support, including technical assistance and capacity-building, and avoid interference in the internal affairs of Iraq and Kuwait. China also supports the Secretary-General’s continued reporting to the Council on progress in implementation.
after.France: France voted in favour of the resolution just adopted by the Council. We welcome its unanimous adoption, which reaffirms the obligations set out in resolution 2107 (2013), in particular regarding missing Kuwaiti and third-country nationals and missing Kuwaiti property, including the national archives. France commends Iraq and Kuwait for their continued cooperation through the tripartite mechanism and with the International Committee of the Red Cross, and we welcome the progress made in locating and repatriating the remains of missing persons. We encourage the Government of Iraq to intensify its efforts and to continue providing full, safe and unhindered access to relevant sites, information and archives, in close cooperation with Kuwait and the tripartite mechanism. France also encourages both countries to pursue constructive dialogue and confidence-building on all outstanding bilateral issues. We reaffirm our commitment to the sovereignty, territorial integrity, political independence and inviolability of Iraq and Kuwait, and we support the Secretary-General’s continued reporting so that the Council may follow progress, including on remaining obstacles and ways to accelerate international technical assistance and capacity-building.
after.Russian Federation: The Russian Federation voted in favour of the draft resolution. We welcome its adoption by consensus. The completion of the mandate of the United Nations Compensation Commission and the dissolution of the Compensation Fund, in accordance with resolution 2621 (2022), have removed an important legacy issue from the Council’s agenda. We note the continued cooperation between Iraq and Kuwait, including through the tripartite mechanism and with the International Committee of the Red Cross, and we commend the practical progress achieved on the humanitarian track, in particular regarding the search for missing Kuwaiti and third-country nationals and missing Kuwaiti property, including the national archives. At the same time, we stress that all efforts in this area must be pursued with full respect for the sovereignty, territorial integrity, political independence and inviolability of Iraq and Kuwait, and without interference in their internal affairs. The Russian Federation supports the continuation of the Secretary-General’s reporting and the provision of international technical assistance and capacity-building to the parties on the basis of their consent and in their interests. We call on Iraq and Kuwait to maintain constructive dialogue and confidence-building and confirm our readiness to continue supporting these efforts in the Security Council.
after.Sierra Leone:
Mr. President,

Sierra Leone welcomes the unanimous adoption of this resolution and voted in favour. We thank the United Kingdom for its efforts in bringing the Council together on this important matter.

Sierra Leone reaffirms the sovereignty, territorial integrity, political independence and inviolability of Iraq and Kuwait, and the importance of non-interference in their internal affairs. We support the full implementation of resolution 2107 (2013) and all relevant resolutions, in particular the obligations to locate, recover and return all missing Kuwaiti and third-country nationals and missing Kuwaiti property, including the national archives.

We commend the continued cooperation between Iraq and Kuwait, including through the tripartite mechanism and the International Committee of the Red Cross, and we encourage both Governments to sustain constructive dialogue and confidence-building. The humanitarian dimension remains central: families have the right to know the fate and whereabouts of their missing loved ones.

Sierra Leone supports the Secretary-General’s continued six-monthly reporting and encourages international technical assistance and capacity-building, as appropriate, to help Iraq and Kuwait achieve further concrete progress. We remain committed to the peaceful settlement of outstanding issues and to the Council’s continued engagement.
after.Slovenia: I thank the President. Slovenia voted in favour of the draft resolution, and we welcome its adoption by consensus. We commend the continued engagement of Iraq and Kuwait, together with the International Committee of the Red Cross and the tripartite mechanism, and we acknowledge the progress made in locating and repatriating the remains of missing persons. At the same time, the humanitarian obligations at the heart of this file remain fully applicable. In particular, Iraq must continue to fulfil its obligations under resolution 2107 (2013) to locate, recover and return all missing Kuwaiti and third-country nationals and missing Kuwaiti property, including the national archives. We call on Iraq to intensify its efforts and to provide full, safe and unhindered access to relevant sites, information and archives. Slovenia stresses the importance of continued confidence-building between Iraq and Kuwait, and of resolving all outstanding bilateral issues peacefully and through dialogue. We support the Secretary-General’s continued six-monthly reporting, including on obstacles and on ways to accelerate progress through international technical assistance and capacity-building. We also reaffirm the sovereignty, territorial integrity, political independence and inviolability of both Iraq and Kuwait. Slovenia remains committed to a humanitarian approach that upholds the right of families to know the fate and whereabouts of their loved ones and that closes this painful chapter through cooperation, international law and multilateral support.
after.Somalia: Somalia voted in favour of this resolution because it affirms the sovereignty, territorial integrity, political independence and inviolability of Iraq and Kuwait and supports the peaceful resolution of outstanding bilateral issues through dialogue and cooperation. We commend the continued engagement of Iraq and Kuwait, together with the International Committee of the Red Cross and the tripartite mechanism, and the progress made in locating and repatriating the remains of missing persons. As a country that has experienced conflict and displacement, Somalia attaches particular importance to the right of families to know the fate and whereabouts of missing persons. We call for full implementation of resolution 2107 (2013), including efforts to locate, recover and return all missing Kuwaiti and third-country nationals and missing Kuwaiti property, including the national archives. We encourage both countries to sustain confidence-building measures and welcome the Secretary-General’s continued six-monthly reporting. Somalia remains committed to the principles of the Charter, including non-interference in internal affairs and the peaceful settlement of disputes.
after.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: Thank you, Mr President. The United Kingdom welcomes the unanimous adoption of the resolution we submitted. The Council’s unity today reflects our shared commitment to the sovereignty, territorial integrity, political independence and inviolability of Iraq and Kuwait, and to the full implementation of resolution 2107 (2013), including on missing Kuwaiti and third-country nationals and missing Kuwaiti property, including the national archives. We thank all Council members for their constructive engagement. We welcome the continued cooperation between Iraq and Kuwait, the International Committee of the Red Cross and the tripartite mechanism, and we encourage Iraq to intensify its efforts, including by providing full, safe and unhindered access to relevant sites, information and archives. The United Kingdom remains committed to supporting this work, continued United Nations reporting and confidence-building between the parties.
after.United States of America: Thank you, Mr. President. The United States welcomes the unanimous adoption of this resolution and thanks the United Kingdom for its leadership as penholder. We reaffirm our support for the sovereignty, territorial integrity, political independence, and inviolability of Iraq and Kuwait. We commend the Governments of Iraq and Kuwait, the International Committee of the Red Cross, and the tripartite mechanism for the progress achieved to date on missing persons and missing property. At the same time, we underscore that Iraq’s obligations under resolution 2107 (2013) remain fully applicable, including the obligations to locate, recover, and return all missing Kuwaiti and third-country nationals and missing Kuwaiti property, including the national archives. We call on Iraq to continue intensifying its efforts and to provide full, safe, and unhindered access to relevant sites, information, and archives. The United States supports continued six-monthly reporting by the Secretary-General and remains committed to constructive support for Iraq and Kuwait as they address these outstanding humanitarian issues through dialogue and confidence-building. Thank you.
